title: HER (hydrogen evolution) reference family
reaction: 2 H+ + 2 e- -> H2 (acidic) | 2 H2O + 2 e- -> H2 + 2 OH- (alkaline)
objective: Optional literature-backed electrocatalyst family for HER cathodes in PEM and AEM/alkaline water electrolyzers. Candidates compare a Pt/C precious-metal anchor with non-noble routes (NiMo alkaline, MoS2 acidic) so the screening can reward either route maturity or non-PGM catalyst economics.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance current stack economics, evidence quality, route maturity, and reported performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward catalyst and electrode cost while preserving route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward stronger literature support and more reproducible electrolyzer-cathode routes.

citations.label: J. Electrochem. Soc. 2005
citations.note: Norskov, Bligaard et al.: trends in the exchange current for HER establishing the canonical HER volcano plot and free-energy descriptor used to rank electrocatalysts.

citations.label: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005
citations.note: Hinnemann, Moses et al.: biomimetic hydrogen evolution showing MoS2 nanoparticles as a non-precious HER catalyst, motivating the active-edge-site picture for sulfide electrocatalysts.

citations.label: Science 2007
citations.note: Jaramillo, Jorgensen, Bonde et al.: identification of MoS2 edge sites as the active surface for electrochemical H2 evolution, establishing the basal-plane vs edge-plane design rule.

citations.label: Nature Materials 2007
citations.note: ORR study on Pt3M alloy surfaces; mechanistic context only, not direct HER or Pt/C electrode-assembly evidence.

citations.label: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2011
citations.note: Li, Wang et al.: MoS2 nanoparticles grown on graphene as an advanced HER electrocatalyst, demonstrating the conductive-support strategy for sulfide active phases.

citations.label: Nature Materials 2013
citations.note: Voiry, Yamaguchi et al.: enhanced HER activity on strained chemically exfoliated WS2 nanosheets, showing how phase and strain engineering activate transition-metal dichalcogenides.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2014
citations.note: Gong, Zhou et al.: nanoscale nickel oxide / nickel heterostructures for active HER electrocatalysis in alkaline electrolyte, an early non-noble alkaline cathode demonstration.

citations.label: Chem. Soc. Rev. 2015
citations.note: Zou and Zhang: comprehensive review of noble-metal-free hydrogen-evolution catalysts for water splitting, organising sulfide, phosphide, carbide, and alloy families.

citations.label: Nature Energy 2016
citations.note: Jiao, Zheng et al.: activity origin and catalyst design principles for electrocatalytic HER on heteroatom-doped graphene, supporting metal-free HER routes.

citations.label: Nature Materials 2016
citations.note: Li, Tsai et al.: activating and optimizing MoS2 basal planes for HER through the formation of strained sulphur vacancies, expanding usable active surface beyond edges.

citations.label: Nature Materials 2016
citations.note: Voiry, Fullon et al.: role of electronic coupling between substrate and 2D MoS2 nanosheets in electrocatalytic hydrogen production, clarifying interfacial charge transfer.

citations.label: Nature Catalysis 2018
citations.note: Zhang, Zhao et al.: single Pt atoms immobilized on an MXene as an efficient HER catalyst, showing the path to ultralow Pt loading on conductive 2D supports.

citations.label: Nature Nanotechnology 2017
citations.note: Ru nanoparticles in a nitrogenated holey C2N framework: abstract-reported overpotentials of 13.5 mV (acid) and 17.0 mV (alkaline) at 10 mA/cm2. SI Table S1 gives 22 mV in acid at 10 mA/cm2; the discrepancy is unresolved in this audit.

citations.label: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2016
citations.note: fcc-structured ruthenium outperforms platinum for alkaline hydrogen evolution.

citations.label: ACS Catal. 2013
citations.note: Unsupported Ni-Mo nanopowders prepared by precipitation/reduction; 6:4 Ni:Mo precursor molar ratio. Table 1 reports 70 mV at 20 mA/cm2 with 1 mg/cm2 in 2 M KOH at 25 C. The COMET 70/30 wt% recipe and electrode defaults remain screening assumptions.

route_templates.name: PEM Pt/C cathode route
postprocess: CCM coating pass on the cathode side
route_templates.route_note: Most transferable PEM electrolyzer cathode basis with mature commercial Pt/C inputs.

route_templates.name: Alkaline NiMo cathode route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Alkaline / AEM electrolyzer cathode coating route
route_templates.route_note: Non-noble alkaline cathode route, mature in industrial alkaline electrolyzers and reasonable for AEM cells.

route_templates.name: MoS2 acidic cathode route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: PEM-style cathode with MoS2 active phase
preprocess: Conductive carbon or MXene support staging
route_templates.route_note: Emerging non-noble PEM cathode option; MoS2 phase control and long-term acidic stability lower route maturity versus Pt/C.

candidates.title: Pt/C HER cathode (PEM)
candidates.summary: Commercial Pt/C cathode used as the baseline PEM-electrolyzer HER anchor.
decision_notes: Most transferable HER cathode basis and the clearest commercial comparison point for PEM electrolyzer stacks.
Economics remain dominated by live Pt price exposure even at low cathode loading.

pricing.note: Live Pt feed with a mild precursor / conversion markup for commercial Pt/C cathode screening.

Carbon support held on an engineering proxy basis in line with the ORR Pt/C convention. Bracketed by public references: UN Comtrade 2024 U.S. carbon-black import unit value ~$1.88/kg (~$0.85/lb rubber grade) and Fuel Cell Store Vulcan XC-72R lab retail ~$950/kg. Bulk conductive/acetylene battery grades cluster at $5,000-7,000/t in marketplace offers (MOQ 1-2 t), the tier between rubber grade and lab retail.

candidates.title: NiMo alkaline HER cathode
candidates.summary: Nickel-molybdenum alloy cathode for alkaline / AEM electrolyzer HER, common in industrial alkaline stacks.
decision_notes: Use this when avoiding PGMs is the program goal and an alkaline / AEM stack is acceptable.
Earth-abundant chemistry keeps catalyst economics low at the cost of slightly higher overpotential than Pt/C.

pricing.note: Live Ni feed with a precursor / conversion markup.
Indexed Mo feed with a precursor / conversion markup for NiMo alloy screening.

candidates.title: MoS2 acidic HER cathode
candidates.summary: MoS2-based cathode targeting non-noble PEM-style HER, leveraging edge-site and basal-plane activation strategies from the literature.
decision_notes: Use when an acidic non-noble HER cathode is desired and the program can absorb lower route maturity for catalyst-economics upside.
Long-term acidic stability and reproducible edge-site population remain the main risks versus the Pt/C anchor.

pricing.note: MoS2 active phase held on a derived screening proxy combining Mo commodity exposure with a sulfide-processing overhead until a cleaner public bulk price is curated.

candidates.title: Ru@C2N pH-universal cathode
candidates.summary: Ruthenium particles in a nitrogenated carbon framework are a literature architecture for hydrogen evolution in acid and base. Relative Ru/Pt cost depends on the selected price basis.
decision_notes: Prices the Ru-for-Pt substitution between the Pt/C baseline and the two non-PGM entries.
C2N is an engineering price proxy. The public supplementary methods identify hexaaminobenzene preparation; no source-matched melamine-to-C2N cost conversion or bulk C2N quotation was verified.

pricing.note: Live Ru feed with a framework-synthesis markup; loading is a screening assumption at the high-dispersion end.
C2N is an engineering price proxy. The public supplementary methods identify hexaaminobenzene preparation; no source-matched melamine-to-C2N cost conversion or bulk C2N quotation was verified.
